Summary of Findings: Three Major
 Takeaways
How Much - To what extent were students impacted
academically by the COVID-19 pandemic?
• The academic impacts of the pandemic were substantial, ranging from
 moderate to very large.
• 2021 ILEARN data indicates substantial academic impact across grades 3
 to 8 in both ELA and Mathematics.
• 2021 WIDA-ACCESS data confirms large academic impacts for most
 English Language Learners.
• In the isolated contexts where modest to no impacts were observed,
 questions about the efficacy of education pre-COVID are a concern.

Summary of Findings: Three Major
 Takeaways
In What - In which content areas were students
academically impacted?
• ILEARN Indiana students experienced large to very large academic
 impacts in math and moderate to large academic impacts in English
 Language Arts.
• WIDA-ACCESS Most Indiana English Language Learners
 experienced large to very large academic impacts in English
 Language Proficiency.

Summary of Findings: Three Major
 Takeaways
Who - Which demographic/academic student groups
experienced academic impact?
• In Grades 3 to 8, academic impacts were of comparable size within content area.
• Student demographic subgroups (e.g., ethnicity) experienced comparable impact
 by grade and content area.
• Student academic subgroups experienced different amounts of academic impact.
 English Language Learners experienced different amounts of impact depending
 upon grade.
• Corporation and school impacts were highly variable with most corporations and
 schools experiencing substantial academic impacts.

Academic Impact & Recovery Time
 How Much? Size of impact is commensurate
 with length of recovery & academic support
 • Recovery is defined as getting back to where students or
 groups of students would be under normal learning
 conditions.
 • Recovery does not imply getting back to proficiency.
 Getting to proficiency would be a higher bar than recovery
 for pre-pandemic, non-proficient students to meet.

Academic Impact & Recovery Time
 How Much? Three Categories
 • “Large” academic impact implies academic recovery exceeding one-
 year and likely requiring supplemental academic support.

 • “Moderate” academic impact implies academic recovery of up to one-
 year and likely requiring some supplemental academic support.

 • “Modest or no” academic impact implies little deviation from what
 was observed historically. Caution in interpreting this group should
 be exercised (discussed later).

Data Sources
Three sources of data used to assess academic impact:
• ILEARN: ELA and Mathematics using both student academic growth and
 student attainment.
• WIDA-ACCESS: English Language Proficiency exam using both
 academic growth and student attainment.
• NWEA-MAP: ELA and Mathematics assessments with less recent data
 for Fall 2020 and Winter 2021 (Grades 1 to 10)
• Currently no data for high school students or student data in other content
 areas.

Specific Areas of Concern
Type 1: Issues due to COVID-19
• Academic impact in mathematics is consistently large and across all
 grades.
• Academic impacts in ELA, though not as large as math, are
 considerable.
• These impacts likely extending across all K-12 grades and to other
 content areas.
• Rates of learning required for recovery are unprecedented at the
 scale required.

Specific Areas of Concern
Type 2: Pre-existing issues identified due to COVID
• There are some large groups of students demonstrating little to no
 academic impact.
• Little to no academic impact for large groups likely brings to light
 ineffectual pre-pandemic performance.
 • High school WIDA-ACCESS growth shows no decline during
 the pandemic.
 • Lowest achievers in some grades and content areas showed
 very little decline during the pandemic.
